claims.title: Right translation on the closure of the generated module
claims.hypotheses: Ψ is the normalized kernel of λ with its Casimir scalar and square integrability, v₀ ≠ 0, and V is the span of the coefficient functions f_u(g) = ⟨v₀,Ψ(g)u⟩.
claims.statement: Right translation is a strongly continuous unitary representation of G on L²(G). It maps the closure H of the module generated by V into itself, so its restriction σ_λ is a unitary representation.
definitions: The layers start at V and add one noncompact derivative at each step; their union is the generated module.

claims.correspondence: Unimodularity gives unitarity. Taylor series of orbits, with the radius from the noncompact layer bound, keep translates of generated vectors in the closure.
claims.review: The rank-one case was checked against the explicit kernel.

claims.title: The Bochner bound for the derivative layers
claims.hypotheses: The hypotheses of the closure hold, λ is strictly decreasing and the opposite-sign gap satisfies h > 2m.
claims.statement: A nonzero compact highest-weight vector of weight μ in layer k+1, orthogonal to layer k, satisfies κ(μ) ≥ κ(Λ) + 2(k+1)(h − m + 1), and μ − Λ is a sum of k+1 noncompact roots. Hence compact highest-weight vectors of weight Λ lie in V and every compact type lies in a bounded layer.
definitions: κ(η) = |η + ρ_c|² − |ρ_c|² is the compact Casimir scalar.
The mixed operator couples one noncompact slot with the lowest type.

claims.correspondence: A new layer vector lifts to a highest-weight tensor. The compact Casimir of the diagonal action splits into a nonnegative slot term, the lowest-type scalar and mixed operators, which the Dirac inequality confines to raising directions.
claims.review: On U(1,1) the tensor of k+1 raising directions and the Dirac contradiction for a lowered vector were computed by hand.

claims.title: Irreducibility, multiplicity one and compact finiteness of the model
claims.hypotheses: The hypotheses of the layer bound hold.
claims.statement: The generated module is irreducible under the derivatives. A compact-equivariant map from the lowest type into the closure with image orthogonal to the lowest type vanishes. The closure has no nontrivial closed invariant subspace, and every finite-dimensional compact-stable subspace of the closure lies in the generated module.

claims.correspondence: Representing vectors of highest-weight functionals on finite-dimensional layers are compact highest-weight vectors of weight Λ, hence lie in the lowest type.
claims.review: The case analysis for an invariant subspace was rechecked against the multiplicity-one statement.

claims.title: The reproducing formula for the coefficient functions
claims.hypotheses: The hypotheses of the layer bound hold and w is the unit highest-weight vector of the lowest type T.
claims.statement: For u, u′ ∈ T and g ∈ G, ⟨f_{u′},R(g)f_u⟩ = ‖f_w‖²⟨u′,Ψ(g)u⟩.
definitions: The Gram identity ⟨f_{u′},f_u⟩ = ‖f_w‖²⟨u′,u⟩ is the case g = 1.

claims.correspondence: The projection of a translate onto V is identified by averaging the residual over K, multiplicity one and Schur orthogonality on K. No orthogonality on G is used.
claims.review: An angular average and an exact radial integral give 4096/78125 for the rank-one coefficient at the displayed group element.

claims.title: The model is the discrete series of parameter λ
claims.hypotheses: λ is a Harish-Chandra parameter with h > max{2m, 16mq + 8√(2q)} and q ≥ 1.
claims.statement: σ_λ is a nonzero irreducible unitary representation with square-integrable coefficients, contains the compact type of highest weight Λ = λ + ρ_n − ρ_c, and that type is minimal in Vogan’s sense. Any representation with these properties is unitarily equivalent to σ_λ.
definitions: Vogan minimality: |Λ + 2ρ_c|² ≤ |μ + 2ρ_c|² for every compact type μ that occurs.

claims.correspondence: One square-integrable coefficient gives all of them in an irreducible representation. Minimality follows from the layer bound, and uniqueness from multiplicity one applied to a direct sum.
claims.review: The minimality inequality was rederived from the layer bound and the bound on ρ_c.

claims.title: The growth bound for smooth vectors and the weighted coefficients
claims.hypotheses: W is a space of smooth functions on G, stable under the compact derivatives, consisting of Casimir eigenfunctions with one eigenvalue, and square integrable with the weight ‖g‖_F^{4a} for some a ≥ 0. The kernel application also assumes ∫‖g‖²_F‖Ψ(g)‖² dg < ∞, supplied by the third decay threshold with s = 2.
claims.statement: Every derivative of a member of W by a word in the E_ab has the same weighted bound, and ∫E_ij F·conj(F′) = sgn(i,j)∫F·conj(E_ji F′). For the kernel model, ‖g‖_F⟨y,R(g)x⟩ is square integrable for all x, y in the generated module.
definitions: T = ∑ sgn(i,j)E_ji E_ij = 2C_K − C, where C_K is the compact Casimir.

claims.correspondence: Cutoffs built from log ‖g‖_F² have derivatives O(1/R). Integration by parts gives a Gårding inequality controlled by T, which preserves the filtration by word length.
claims.review: On U(1,1) the identity ∑‖E_ij f‖² = ⟨f,Tf⟩ was checked for f = g₁₁^{−k} by explicit integrals.
